findings.title: Cleanup-empty checkpoints skip op/reason assertions
findings.detail: In TestArchivedPROffersThePushUntilItIsDone (also at line 710), the checks `len(got) != 0` / `len(again) != 0` read `o["cleanup"]` without first asserting `o["op"] == "stop"` and `o["reason"] == stopArchived` (as the earlier and later checkpoints in the same test do, e.g. lines 673-674, 683-684, 722-723). cleanupOf silently returns an empty slice when the "cleanup" key is absent or of the wrong shape, so if `next` regressed to returning a different op entirely at these points, the 'nothing offered' assertions would pass anyway, masking the regression in exactly the rows this test exists to pin (G7's zero-cleanup cases).

findings.title: preparePushPR's new commitBundle error path is untested
findings.detail: The new `if _, _, err = commitBundle(ctx, r.ws, r.bdir, r.slug, "pr body"); err != nil { return err }` propagates a commit failure exactly like the pre-existing read/write failures preparePushPR already returns, but no test forces commitBundle to fail here (e.g. a broken repo/lock) to confirm the error surfaces through preparePushPR and ultimately fails `run` the same way assertPreparePushPRRefuses covers for the spec/goals reads. The codebase already has a pattern for simulating git-commit failures (internal/cli/archive_test.go's TestArchiveCommitIsRetriedAfterASoftReset) that could have been reused here.

findings.title: recordReviewDeadline's failure path is never exercised
findings.detail: The new block `if p := f.getenv("TAKT_FAKE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_FILE"); p != "" { if err := recordReviewDeadline(ctx, p); err != nil { return errorResult(...) } }` (fake.go:45-49) has no test that makes the write fail (e.g. a path in a nonexistent directory), so the errorResult branch this new code adds is untested. TestBackendFallbackMatchesTheShippedDefault only exercises the success path via a valid t.TempDir() file.

findings.title: Added assertion re-invokes commitBundle rather than checking preparePushPR's own call
findings.detail: Lines 188-191 call `commitBundle(context.Background(), r.ws, r.bdir, r.slug, "pr body")` a second, separate time to assert `committed==false`. Since `r.ws` is the same zero-value workspace (Dir.InRepo false) that preparePushPR's own internal commitBundle call at line 171 already ran through without error, this second call is a fresh, independent invocation rather than an observation of what preparePushPR actually did — it documents commitBundle's no-op behaviour in isolation more than it verifies the integration point, though it does satisfy the brief's explicit request for 'one assertion making that explicit'.
